summary.description: What you did, in prose. Name the files you touched and the approach you took, so a reader who never opens the diff knows what landed.

deferred.description: Work inside the brief that you did not do, and why. Empty string only if you did all of it.

verification.description: Every command you ran to check the work. A claim with no command behind it belongs in summary, not here.

command.description: The command as you ran it, verbatim.

outcome.description: not_run means you intended this check but could not run it; say why in detail.

detail.description: Counts, the failing assertion, or the error text. Enough for a reader to judge the outcome without rerunning it.

name.description: The branch you actually created. Empty string if you never got as far as creating one.

base_sha.description: The commit on the base branch that you branched from.

head_sha.description: The tip of your branch after the last commit.

pushed.description: True only after a push that git reported as successful. The workspace is deleted after the run, so an unpushed commit is lost work.

pull_request_url.description: URL of the draft pull request. Empty string if it was not created.

files_changed.description: One entry per file in the diff between base_sha and head_sha. Read it out of git diff --numstat rather than from memory.

error.description: Empty string when you finished the brief and pushed the branch. Otherwise what blocked you, what you tried, and what state you left behind. Blank this field only on success; a half-finished run that reports no error is worse than one that reports the truth.
